rows.title: 10 big promises Colorado Gov. Jared Polis kept in his first term — and some he hasn’t (so far)
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun kept track of more than 100 of the Democrats’ 2018 campaign promises. We evaluated about 20 as he runs for reelection in November.

rows.title: How Colorado plans to cover 99% of the state with super-fast internet
rows.standfirst: Brandy Reitter, who experiences subpar broadband service while living in Eagle, is leading the Broadband Office’s effort to spend nearly $1 billion in federal funds to get Coloradans access to fiber internet

rows.title: Oil and gas drilling plan OK’d for 55 square miles in Aurora, including area where 12,500 homes are planned
rows.standfirst: State regulators confirmed Crestone Peak’s Box Elder drilling plan for 55 square miles of land the energy company has been working on since 2020, saying Colorado’s new permitting process is “workable, protective”

rows.title: Time is running out on Colorado’s rent assistance program
rows.standfirst: Thousands of Colorado households — and their landlords — benefited from the $690 million in federal Emergency Rental Assistance. The state’s application portal closes Nov. 15.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s job growth isn’t all that’s shrinking. So is its population growth.
rows.standfirst: The state’s population grew just 0.5% last year, the slowest since 2011. Plus: Twitter job cuts, interest rates and more.

rows.title: What have we learned about the arguments for and against legalized marijuana in the past 10 years?
rows.standfirst: As we look back on a decade since Colorado’s landmark vote on legalized cannabis, we assess how arguments from both sides of the debate have borne out

rows.title: To keep people from returning to jail, Mesa County follows other communities’ reentry roadmap
rows.standfirst: Many people transitioning from jail or prison struggle to reenter society without support. Mesa County’s new program helps with housing, jobs, transportation and mental health services.

rows.title: “The future of housing” takes shape at Buena Vista factory
rows.standfirst: A housing crisis solution with modular homes, philanthropy, unique lending and free land is threatened by local zoning and code regulations

rows.title: Colorado voters poised to cut the state’s income tax rate for the second time in two years
rows.standfirst: Proposition 121 slashes the rate to 4.4% from 4.55% starting in tax year 2022. Another income tax measure, Proposition GG, passed Tuesday as well.

rows.title: Push for wine sales in Colorado grocery, convenience stores is too close to call as voters reject two other booze ballot measures
rows.standfirst: Measures that would have dramatically changed the way Coloradans buy alcohol were failing Tuesday night, even with $30 million in campaign donations

rows.title: What’s Working: People with a felony record are getting more opportunities from Colorado employers
rows.standfirst: Workers with a felony in their past could really use Honest Jobs. Plus: Denver’s slowing inflation rate puts it among “least rising” in U.S., fraud updates and more!

rows.title: Colorado voters approve ballot measure setting aside nearly $300 million each year for affordable housing
rows.standfirst: Proposition 123 will set aside up to 0.1% of taxable income each year for affordable housing. That’s estimated to be $145 million in the current fiscal year — which ends June 30, 2023 — and $290 million in 2023-24 and subsequent fiscal years.

rows.title: Oil, gas, coal mining on federal land in Colorado generates $393M in revenue, most in 14 years
rows.standfirst: Increasing royalties for the first time since the 1920s is credited for some of the extra revenue due to Colorado governments this fiscal year

rows.title: Colorado sees big increase in new businesses after filing fees drop to $1
rows.standfirst: But the Secretary of State’s third-quarter data showed more companies dissolving or are late in filing periodic reports, which has economists concerned.

rows.title: Late bidder, recreation groups look to derail Denver-based company’s bid for San Luis & Rio Grande Railroad
rows.standfirst: San Luis Valley Great Outdoors objects to Omnitrax plan to buy the San Luis & Rio Grande Railroad

rows.title: Western Slope voters overwhelmingly passed taxes on short-term rentals to fund affordable housing
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s Western Slope communities could generate about $40 million in new tax revenue from vacation rentals to support affordable housing

rows.title: What’s Working: Thanksgiving meal inflation is higher in Colorado than U.S.
rows.standfirst: Plus: Unemployment rate increases to 3.6% but troubled tech sector isn’t necessarily to blame, new businesses on the rise, more!

rows.title: Xcel’s $32M plan for Sloan Lake area ignites debate over Colorado’s energy future
rows.standfirst: Critics say Xcel Energy’s push to supply natural gas to 6,800 new customers in Denver, Edgewater and Lakewood runs afoul of Denver’s plans to reduce natural gas consumption

rows.title: Why the price of eggs went up in Colorado this year
rows.standfirst: Avian flu has killed off 85% of Colorado’s egg-laying hens amid high inflation. The industry says there’s no egg shortage — just higher costs for everyone.

rows.title: After fire, a Native American-inclusive tent community races to rebuild before winter
rows.standfirst: Thirty-seven people were displaced and 16 people lost everything they owned when a fire tore through a city-sanctioned tent community near Denver Health

rows.title: How two brothers plan to save the world by packing a whole farm into shipping containers on a Denver used car lot
rows.standfirst: Ullr’s Garden grows tangy artisanal arugula in climate-controlled trailers just off Broadway, on 5 gallons of water a day

rows.title: Silver dream goes bust: Ouray mine faces lawsuits for $10M in unpaid bills
rows.standfirst: After big plans to revive the famed Revenue Mine, the current owners Ouray Silver Mines shut down and are in receivership after defaulting on $28 million loan

rows.title: “Golden Girls” find community and safety in Western Slope shelter
rows.standfirst: Women account for about 35% of people who are homeless in Mesa County, where the wait for subsidized housing is 3 years.

rows.title: Old motels are putting a dent in Colorado’s homelessness crisis after serving as emergency shelters during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Already this fall, the city of Denver has helped nonprofits buy three motels that eventually will provide hundreds of housing units for those living on the streets

rows.title: RTD hires its first homeless outreach coordinator to visit stations, offer services to those illegally camped
rows.standfirst: RTD has one worker who visits light-rail and bus stations in eight counties, offering housing and other services to those in need.

rows.title: Colorado’s second-largest electric provider is set to lose 25% of its revenue as customers flee
rows.standfirst: Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association is at a crossroads as its 42 rural co-ops look to generate more of their own electricity or buy it on the open market
